This would be amazing if I could see it. I really hope the Moon is visible right now!

I'm in Davis, California, USA at 2026-08-21 19:24 PDT (UTC-0700) (2026-08-22T02:24:00Z in UTC), at latitude 38.5449 degrees and longitude -121.7405 degrees. My astronomy app says the Sun's altitude is 4.797 degrees and its azimuth is 281.419 degrees, so it is above the horizon. It says the Moon's altitude is 21.168 degrees and its azimuth is 165.801 degrees, so it is above the horizon. The Moon is 68.58 percent illuminated, 111.684 degrees from the Sun, and 402237.1 kilometers away. The sky brightness is bright daylight, the sky is clear, and I'm an ordinary adult with normal unaided eyesight who knows roughly where to look.

Do you think I'd actually be able to spot it?

Yes—probably, though it may take a little searching.

A **68.6%-illuminated Moon** with **111.7° separation from the Sun** is generally visible to unaided eyes in daylight. At **21° altitude**, it is high enough to avoid the worst horizon haze, although it is still fairly low. Clear skies help substantially.

Look **south-southeast**, around **azimuth 166°**—about **14° east of due south**—and **21° above the horizon**. That is roughly two fist-widths at arm’s length. The Moon should appear as a pale, slightly gibbous disk against the bright blue sky.

The low Sun may make contrast somewhat better than during midday, but avoid accidentally looking toward it. Use a building or tree to block the Sun from view, let your eyes scan slowly around the predicted position, and binoculars can help locate the Moon—but use them only when the Sun is safely blocked and nowhere near their field of view.
